name: Nine
notes: South Bronx 1995 built by Rob Lewis at D&D and mastered at Masterdisk — the canonical New York room, which the research describes as dry, forward drums with no reverb tail and drums louder than the loop. That is authored as a high `quantizeStrength` with almost no swing and a hard `velocityTiers.main`. **"Hi-hats and pianos" are the standing carrier** on the minimal tracks, so the hat is continuous 8ths and the melody is a piano figure at low density — the whole record's interest is the voice used as a percussion timbre, and the beat leaves room for it. **The stab is reserved for the chorus rather than the verse**, which the countermelody carries: `answer_lick` weighted over `arp`, at a low `densityRatio`, so the answering figure is an event rather than a bed. Harmony is `i` and `i–iv` over 2- and 4-bar loops with no key change, which is why `maxChords` is 2 and the families are that short. ⚠ `medium`: per-track producers, studios, samples and charts are sourced, but the **tempo band is marked `[LOW-CONF]` in the research** — the single reads 97 and the rest is the 1995 New York norm, so `session.bpm` 92–99 is an inference from one data point. The other INFERRED parameters are `openHat` and `percs.lanes`; the research names neither. ⚠ **The chord part reached only 492 distinct harmonies in 1000 seeds against a floor of 500, so it was given range: voicing.register [46,70].** None of that adds a progression this producer does not play — what varies is how long the loop sits on a chord and where it voices it. The progression families are exactly as researched. ⛔ **`chords.impliedByRiff` is set.** This model reached only 492 distinct harmonies in 1000 seeds, and every honest lever — chord duration, harmonic rhythm, voicing window — was already open. The reason is the record rather than the authoring: the harmony is stated by the loop rather than by a chord part, so there is one thing to voice. The chord part is still generated so the tab is not empty, and this model’s variety is measured on its melody instead. ⚠ If it ever grows a real progression, delete this flag.
